Absolutely hilarious. I'll never understand why people don't question why apps like Messenger default to sending your exact location to everyone you talk to. All it takes is a compromised account and you have a virtual honeypot of very precious information. Add on to that the fact that most people use their full real name on their Facebook profiles and even those who aren't constantly updating their status or uploading pictures are usually offering up at least some amount of information about themselves whether they know it or not. I'm not one to be viciously paranoid about the security of my data because I realize that the people who want it are going to get it and the best I can hope for is to make it inconvenient for them or dissuade them all together. That said, I don't think constantly spewing data all over the place with no regards to how it is stored, who is allowed to see it, who maintains ownership of it, how long it is retained, or how it is transmitted and when, isn't a good foundation for our increasingly "smart" lives.

These days everything from your television to your showerhead is connected to the internet and gathering data about you. Sure, it enriches our lives (sometimes), but at what cost? In a world where data security is becoming more and more important and we are starting to see much more serious threats at the very foundation of our current systems, how do we balance the need for information with the safety of it after it leaves our hands?

This is going to be the next big problem.
